answer: Sybil resistance can work by tying identity to a costly physical anchor: each agent stakes a bonded hardware token whose unique thermal pulse is logged on a shared ledger. Forging duplicates requires replicating that signature on certified basalt-based substrates, an expense exceeding any reward from fake identities. Peers also cross-check a random whisper challenge each epoch, so a cloned node cannot echo the correct low-noise pattern without the original device, making mass impersonation economically irrational.
